explanation: Se evalúa de izquierda a derecha: 10 + 20 = 30 (ambos son números); luego 30 + "Java" ya es concatenación, y lo que sigue se concatena como texto: 10 y 20, sin sumar.
explanation_en: It is evaluated left to right: 10 + 20 = 30 (both are numbers); then 30 + "Java" is already concatenation, and what follows is concatenated as text: 10 and 20, without adding.

explanation: == compara referencias. Java reutiliza objetos Integer entre -128 y 127 (caché de autoboxing); 130 crea objetos distintos. Para comparar valores usa equals.
explanation_en: == compares references. Java reuses Integer objects between -128 and 127 (autoboxing cache); 130 creates distinct objects. To compare values use equals.

explanation: i++ devuelve el valor viejo (5) y luego incrementa i a 6, pero la asignación i = ... escribe ese 5 encima. Resultado: 5.
explanation_en: i++ returns the old value (5) and then increments i to 6, but the assignment i = ... writes that 5 on top. Result: 5.

explanation: Da true en Java 17/21 porque el substring vacío reutiliza el literal "", pero es un detalle de implementación. La lección: nunca compares Strings con ==; usa equals.
explanation_en: It prints true on Java 17/21 because the empty substring reuses the literal "", but it is an implementation detail. The lesson: never compare Strings with ==; use equals.

explanation: "a" + "b" es una constante en tiempo de compilación y apunta al mismo literal. new String(...) y la concatenación con una variable en ejecución crean objetos nuevos. intern() devuelve el literal del pool.
explanation_en: "a" + "b" is a compile-time constant and points to the same literal. new String(...) and concatenation with a variable at run time create new objects. intern() returns the pool literal.

explanation: double usa binario: 0.1 y 0.2 no son exactos. Compara con tolerancia (Math.abs(a - b) < 1e-9) o usa BigDecimal para dinero.
explanation_en: double is binary: 0.1 and 0.2 are not exact. Compare with a tolerance (Math.abs(a - b) < 1e-9) or use BigDecimal for money.

explanation: 'a' + 1 promueve a int (97 + 1 = 98). La asignación compuesta c += 1 hace un cast implícito a char, por eso queda 'b'.
explanation_en: 'a' + 1 is promoted to int (97 + 1 = 98). The compound assignment c += 1 does an implicit cast to char, so it ends up as 'b'.

explanation: List.of crea una lista inmutable: add, remove o set lanzan UnsupportedOperationException. Arrays.asList tampoco permite agregar ni quitar.
explanation_en: List.of creates an immutable list: add, remove or set throw UnsupportedOperationException. Arrays.asList does not allow adding or removing either.

explanation: int no lanza error al desbordar: da la vuelta al mínimo. Para detectarlo usa Math.addExact (lanza ArithmeticException) o long.
explanation_en: int does not raise an error on overflow: it wraps around to the minimum. To detect it use Math.addExact (throws ArithmeticException) or long.

explanation: finally se ejecuta antes de que el método devuelva el valor. Primero imprime "finally" y después main imprime 1.
explanation_en: finally runs before the method returns its value. It first prints "finally" and then main prints 1.

explanation: Math.round redondea hacia +infinito en los empates (floor(x + 0.5)): 2.5 -> 3 y -2.5 -> -2.
explanation_en: Math.round rounds toward +infinity on ties (floor(x + 0.5)): 2.5 -> 3 and -2.5 -> -2.

explanation: byte va de -128 a 127. 200 se trunca a los 8 bits bajos (11001000), que en complemento a dos es -56.
explanation_en: byte ranges from -128 to 127. 200 is truncated to the low 8 bits (11001000), which in two's complement is -56.

explanation: Las operaciones intermedias (peek, map) no se ejecutan hasta que hay una operación terminal (collect, forEach, count...). Aquí no hay terminal, así que peek nunca imprime.
explanation_en: Intermediate operations (peek, map) do not run until there is a terminal operation (collect, forEach, count...). Here there is none, so peek never prints.

explanation: Java 21 estabiliza el pattern matching en switch. Los casos se evalúan en orden: 42 es Integer y cumple la guarda i > 40.
explanation_en: Java 21 finalizes pattern matching in switch. Cases are evaluated in order: 42 is an Integer and satisfies the guard i > 40.

explanation: Un record genera equals, hashCode y toString por valor, así que equals da true. == sigue comparando referencias (false). toString imprime P[x=1].
explanation_en: A record generates equals, hashCode and toString by value, so equals gives true. == still compares references (false). toString prints P[x=1].

explanation: En el operador ternario con Integer e int, Java aplica promoción numérica y hace unboxing de x. Como x es null, lanza NullPointerException.
explanation_en: In the ternary operator with Integer and int, Java applies numeric promotion and unboxes x. Since x is null, it throws NullPointerException.

explanation: Con un int literal se llama remove(int index): quita el elemento de la posición 1 (el 2), no el valor 1. Para quitar por valor usa l.remove(Integer.valueOf(1)).
explanation_en: With an int literal, remove(int index) is called: it removes the element at position 1 (the 2), not the value 1. To remove by value use l.remove(Integer.valueOf(1)).

explanation: Java 21 agrega SequencedCollection: reversed(), getFirst() y getLast() en List, Deque, LinkedHashSet, etc.
explanation_en: Java 21 adds SequencedCollection: reversed(), getFirst() and getLast() on List, Deque, LinkedHashSet, etc.

explanation: Los arreglos no sobrescriben equals/hashCode: comparan por identidad. Por eso un HashSet<int[]> no encuentra otro arreglo con el mismo contenido. Usa List<Integer> o Arrays.equals/hashCode.
explanation_en: Arrays do not override equals/hashCode: they compare by identity. That is why a HashSet<int[]> does not find another array with the same content. Use List<Integer> or Arrays.equals/hashCode.

explanation: final impide reasignar la referencia, no modificar el objeto. Para una lista realmente inmutable usa List.of o Collections.unmodifiableList.
explanation_en: final prevents reassigning the reference, not modifying the object. For a truly immutable list use List.of or Collections.unmodifiableList.
